assignments.reason: The ability to build a house (יכול לבנות בית) is essentially the actualization of wisdom in the physical domain — 'be-chokhmah yibaneh bayit' (Proverbs 24:3). Its essential nature is the capacity that Binah/sekhel grants: when one possesses the sheltering wisdom of the Sukkah, one can build properly. This is the same domain as bayit (house), already in Package 1 via additions, and as the Sukkah-Binah cluster itself. The concept represents wisdom made manifest in construction — it belongs to the good Sukkah/Binah domain by its very nature as wisdom-enabled building.

Mikneihu (his livestock) represents the physical, material domain of sustenance and livelihood that depends on the Sukkah's sheltering Binah for its survival. By essential nature it is a neutral object — the animals themselves are neither holy nor evil, but are the natural world that the Sukkah-Binah framework sustains. The Torah explicitly says 'the Sukkah is for his livestock' (u-le-mikneihu asah sukkot), placing mikneihu within the Sukkah's domain of care. As the object of Binah's maternal protection (Imma di-mesakhekha al banin), livestock belongs structurally within the Sukkah/Binah package as the entity being sheltered, with neutral polarity since it is the recipient rather than the source of holiness.
